override.reason: Approved by the user in chat on 2026-11-09 after all three code review rounds. The final round was changes_requested with two MED findings on inputs Vibe does not write: a sub-table header with # or ] inside quotes, and a server name containing the other quote character. The build gate also remains failed: the shared helper and its one-path import allowance have no LLD, and the writers' existing line-by-line reading can misread section-like text inside a multi-line string. The user accepted these limits; a follow-up is to move the writers to a real TOML parser.

meta.triageRationale: Small bugfix ISSUE-b902426092868097: two writers append a server section without accounting for the inline list that Vibe saves.

body.focus: Registering the insrc server in a Vibe config that holds a top-level inline mcp_servers list produces a valid TOML file, from both the VS Code plugin (vscode-plugin/src/hosts/toml-mcp-writer.ts) and the daemon (upsertVibeProjectServer in src/daemon/mcp-register.ts). Every server already in the inline list and every other setting is kept, and insrc is registered once. Registering again changes nothing. Where a writer cannot safely bring a config into a valid form, it leaves the file untouched and reports the failure instead of writing an invalid file.
body.summary: Both Vibe config writers now move an inline mcp_servers list into [[mcp_servers]] tables before adding the insrc server, through one shared helper, and leave a config they cannot fix untouched. An inline entry whose name is not a plain quoted string, whose keys use escapes, or which spans lines is refused rather than converted. The user chose to keep the shared helper.
